items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I gigged with Peek-a-Boo twice and both times it was really enjoyable.

ctx.x: few with him. There are many name musicians in the 20s and 30s that gigged at one time with Fernand; Benny Carter, Rex Stewart, Bobby Starke, etc. When I gigged with Fernand, I met one of the greatest alto sax men in the business. His name was Hilton Jefferson. Jeff was a very quiet man but he made his horn talk for him and all the musicians loved him.

Another musician that always had the highest paid gigs was a drummer named Peek-a-Boo Jimmy. Peek-a-Boo had played with James P. Johnson, Willie 'The Lion' Smith and 'Lucky' Roberts in the days before I even dreamed of going to New York. I gigged with Peek-a-Boo twice and both times it was really enjoyable. The music we played was not very jazzy because Jimmy was a drummer who had lost sight of what the other drummers were doing. And most of the musicians he hired were a certain age and not up to date on jazz…

But Jimmy was in with the rich folks downtown and he played many high society functions. The first one I did with him was a stag party for some business men who had rented a Hudson River cruising boat and invited about 400 men to cruise up the Hudson. We played but there was no dancing as there were no women to dance with. Finally we docked somewhere and everybody went ashore where a big picnic with all kinds of seafood and kegs of beer were waiting for everyone including the band. The committee of this outing…

ctx.x: The war had not changed naything in Kokke since I was there the summer of 1938. Everything went well until the last night when Don Byas went into one of his acts after the last show. Of course, we all had quite a few drinks and were feeling no pains. I had already left the casino when thiks incident happened, but I was told by one of the musicians that Don was high and in the process of changing his clothes, he decided to chase one of the Bluebell girls that had passed his lodge when the door was open. The big thing in jazz from the 8th of May until the 15th was the jazz festival that Charles Delaunay organized in collaboration with Frank Bauer, Eddie Barclay and Jacques Souplet. Sidney Bechet and Charlie(the Bird) Parker were the stars, but there were other musicians that were already in the limelight, whose names were to become much better known than they were in 1949. The American musicians presented at this festival were Bechet, Parker, "Big Chief" Russell Moore, Oran "Hot Lips" Page, Kenny Dorham, Tommie…

Jazz was jumping in Paris that week at the Salle Pleyel and jazz fans from different countries (mostly those who had musicians that were favoured in the places they were from) were here to take in the festival and all the jazz clubs were jumping and especially the club St. Germain des Pres on the left bank of Paris, because the American musicians and some from other countries would go jamming after the nightly concerts or on nights when they did not have to appear with Rostaing(clarinet) Braslavsky(clarinet)…
